logic_node.action: Measure BNP or NT-proBNP to support diagnosis or exclusion of HF
logic_node.action_detail: In patients presenting with dyspnea, measurement of BNP or NT-proBNP is useful to support a diagnosis or exclusion of HF. Provides incremental diagnostic value when cause of dyspnea is unclear and physical examination is equivocal. Higher sensitivity than specificity in emergency settings; more useful for ruling out HF than ruling in.

source_text: In patients presenting with dyspnea, measurement of B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) or N-terminal prohormone of B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) is useful to support a diagnosis or exclusion of HF.

logic_node.action: Measure BNP or NT-proBNP for risk stratification in chronic HF
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with chronic HF, measurements of BNP or NT-proBNP levels are recommended for risk stratification. Higher levels are associated with greater risk for adverse short- and long-term outcomes including all-cause and cardiovascular death and major cardiovascular events.

source_text: In patients with chronic HF, measurements of BNP or NT-proBNP levels are recommended for risk stratification.

logic_node.action: Measure BNP or NT-proBNP at admission for prognosis
logic_node.action_detail: In patients hospitalized for HF, measurement of BNP or NT-proBNP levels at admission is recommended to establish prognosis. Higher levels are associated with greater risk for adverse short- and long-term outcomes including all-cause and cardiovascular death.

source_text: In patients hospitalized for HF, measurement of BNP or NT-proBNP levels at admission is recommended to establish prognosis.

logic_node.action: Screen with BNP or NT-proBNP followed by team-based care to prevent HF
logic_node.action_detail: In patients at risk of developing HF, BNP or NT-proBNP-based screening followed by team-based care including a cardiovascular specialist can be useful to prevent development of LV dysfunction or new-onset HF. In STOP-HF trial, participants with BNP >= 50 pg/mL underwent echocardiography and referral to cardiovascular specialist.

source_text: In patients at risk of developing HF, BNP or NT-proBNP-based screening followed by team-based care, including a cardiovascular specialist, can be useful to prevent the development of LV dysfunction or new-onset HF.

logic_node.action: Measure predischarge BNP or NT-proBNP to inform trajectory and postdischarge prognosis
logic_node.action_detail: In patients hospitalized for HF, a predischarge BNP or NT-proBNP level can be useful to inform the trajectory of the patient and establish a postdischarge prognosis. Patients in whom levels decreased with treatment had better outcomes than those without changes or with a biomarker rise. However, targeting a certain threshold or relative change has not been consistently shown to improve outcomes.

source_text: In patients hospitalized for HF, a predischarge BNP or NT-proBNP level can be useful to inform the trajectory of the patient and establish a postdischarge prognosis.

logic_node.action: Do not use BNP and NT-proBNP values interchangeably
logic_node.action_detail: BNP and NT-proBNP levels are similar in utility, and either can be used in patient care settings, but their respective absolute values and cut-points must not be used interchangeably. Obesity is associated with lower levels of BNP and NT-proBNP, reducing diagnostic sensitivity.

source_text: BNP and NT-proBNP levels are similar, and either can be used in patient care settings as long as their respective absolute values and cut-points are not used interchangeably.

logic_node.action: Use BNP threshold >= 50 pg/mL to trigger echocardiography and specialist referral
logic_node.action_detail: In patients at risk of HF (hypertension, diabetes, or known vascular disease but without established LV systolic dysfunction or symptomatic HF), a BNP level >= 50 pg/mL should trigger echocardiography and referral to a cardiovascular specialist, per STOP-HF trial protocol.

source_text: Participants in the intervention group with BNP levels >= 50 pg/mL underwent echocardiography and referral to a cardiovascular specialist.
